corrections.before: A dummy of the wrong layer or an electrically floating active dummy is not equivalent to the characterized boundary environment.
corrections.after: A dummy whose geometry, layer or bias differs from the qualified construction does not establish the required boundary environment. Some qualified dummy structures are intentionally floating.
corrections.reason: A floating dummy is not universally invalid; qualification is structure-specific.

corrections.before: For a simple single-branch model, gₘ,eff≈gₘ/(1+gₘRₛ); the review analyzes actual unit-current distribution through the array.
corrections.after: For a simple single-branch model, gₘ,eff≈gₘ/(1+gₘRₛ). This closed form is our derivation from i=gₘ(vin−iRₛ), neglecting output conductance and body effect and assuming the branch current is the source-resistor current. The review’s Eq. (25) relates effective transconductance to local source voltage; its array analysis uses the actual unit-current distribution.
corrections.reason: Separate the source equation from our simplified closed-form derivation and state its electrical assumptions.

They describe a linear RC network with defined reference/boundary nodes; ideal voltage sources or inductors require additional variables or boundary treatment. corrections.after: {{cite:topological:137:Chapter 3, §§3.4–3.5, hierarchical alternatives, PDF pp. 137–147}} {{cite:topological:191:Chapter 4, §4.5.4, placement/global-route integration, PDF pp. 191–193}}

corrections.before: learn a graph-based distribution related to performance, cheaply propose width assignments, then route/extract/simulate finalists.
corrections.after: learn a graph-based classifier at a chosen performance threshold, cheaply propose width assignments, then route/extract/simulate finalists.
corrections.reason: WAGN is a threshold classifier, not a learned full performance distribution.

corrections.before: The learned cumulative probability P(FOM<T) is a different output from a deterministic FOM regression; preserve that distinction in the evaluator interface. {{cite:todaes:6:Graph and learning model, PDF pp. 6–12}}
corrections.after: The manuscript denotes its soft classification output P(FOM<T) for a user-specified threshold. A single-threshold score supplies neither a full cumulative distribution nor a calibrated manufacturing-failure probability. It also differs from FOM regression. Preserve these distinctions in the evaluator interface. {{cite:todaes:8:§4.2, graph features, PDF p. 8}} {{cite:todaes:10:§4.3–4.5, Eqs. (17)–(19), classification output/training, PDF pp. 10–11}}
corrections.reason: Correct the implication that the model predicts a full CDF or statistical yield, and pinpoint its definition.

corrections.before: The final output is P(FOM<T): a probability of belonging to the unsatisfactory class, not a prediction of gain in dB or delay in seconds.
corrections.after: The manuscript denotes the final soft classification output P(FOM<T) for one user-specified threshold. It estimates class membership; the reported classification experiments do not establish probability calibration, a full performance distribution or manufacturing yield. It is not a prediction of gain in dB or delay in seconds.
corrections.reason: Separate the author’s probabilistic notation from evidence of calibration or process yield.

corrections.before: It predicts the probability that a normalized FOM is below a threshold.
corrections.after: It produces a soft classification score denoted as the probability that a normalized FOM is below one chosen threshold. Calibration and manufacturing yield are not established by that notation.
corrections.reason: Qualify WAGN probability language consistently.

corrections.before: {{cite:topological:279:Constraint verification discussion, Chapter 7}}
corrections.after: {{cite:topological:291:Chapter 7, §7.4.5, metaverification, PDF pp. 291–293}} {{cite:topological:296:§7.5.2, conflict checking, PDF pp. 296–298}} The distinction between a failed search and a proof of infeasibility is our methodological qualification.
corrections.reason: Use actual metaverification and conflict-checking sections and distinguish our proof-scope guidance.

corrections.before: Current per drawn width is a process-specific surrogate, not volumetric current density.
corrections.after: Current per drawn width is a process-specific surrogate rather than cross-sectional current density in A/m².
corrections.reason: Current density J in A/m² is current per cross-sectional area, not per volume.

corrections.before: Shared trunks carry the sum of downstream currents for each relevant scenario; terminal current is not automatically the current of every segment.
corrections.after: For a tree, shared trunks carry the signed sum of downstream load currents, including interconnect shunt/displacement currents where relevant. Meshed nets require a network solution; one terminal current is not automatically every segment’s current.
corrections.reason: KCL subtree sum needs tree topology and all branch loads; transient interconnect currents cannot be silently omitted.

corrections.before: Thermal noise sets another lower bound on unit size. The familiar kT/C variance is a useful equilibrium estimate for a sampled node under a simple switch-capacitor model. A real charge-redistribution network has several noise sources and transfer factors.
corrections.after: Thermal noise sets another conditional lower bound on unit size. Independent derivation, with a source gap: for one ideal linear capacitor fully equilibrated through resistance at temperature T, classical equipartition assigns its fluctuating voltage energy ½C·Var(v)=½kBT, giving Var(v)=kBT/C. The assumptions are thermal equilibrium, a classical frequency range and an ideal isolated sample after equilibration; finite settling, correlated sampling and complete converter topology change the result. No exact kT/C passage was located in the supplied PDFs, so do not attribute this equation to the DAC paper. A real charge-redistribution network has several noise sources and transfer factors.
corrections.reason: Show the kT/C derivation and disclose that its foundational equilibrium premise has no pinpoint citation in the supplied corpus.

corrections.before: An ideal resistor's classical one-sided open-circuit voltage-noise density is 4k<sub>B</sub>TR V²/Hz within that model's frequency range.
corrections.after: An ideal resistor's classical one-sided open-circuit voltage-noise density is 4kBTR V²/Hz within that model's frequency range. This is a foundational Johnson–Nyquist law; no exact derivation or equation locator was found in the supplied corpus. See the provenance gap and conditional derivation before citing it.
corrections.reason: Avoid treating the uncited Johnson–Nyquist foundation as a checked source claim.

theory_records.title: First moments and first-order performance
theory_records.claim: Coincident normalized x/y centroids remove linear spatial parameter mismatch; translating parameter mismatch into performance uses a separate sensitivity approximation.
theory_records.assumptions: Equal-unit or explicitly normalized additive responses; shared parameter field; circuit linearization valid locally.

theory_records.title: Centroid does not equal device environment
theory_records.claim: WPE, LOD, OD dimensions and gate pitch can shift device parameters even when centroids coincide.
theory_records.assumptions: Relevant process/LDE model; review’s identical-unit simplifications presume its row, pitch and diffusion-sharing construction.

theory_records.title: Pattern choice is conditional
theory_records.claim: The OTA/comparator cases show circumstances in which clustered/interdigitated patterns outperform some CC structures.
theory_records.assumptions: Reported device/circuit/process assumptions; not a universal CC prohibition or a portable size threshold.

theory_records.title: MOS internal topology and source paths
theory_records.claim: Half-diffusion graphs/Euler paths express compatible sharing; source-current distribution and route resistance affect array transconductance.
theory_records.assumptions: Keep actual net labels and unit paths; generalized routing acceptance is a handbook adaptation.

theory_records.title: MOM unit construction exposes different parasitics
theory_records.claim: MOM finger/sandwich/pillar/mortise-tenon constructions trade density and terminal coupling.
theory_records.assumptions: A source-specific advanced-node comparison; selecting a qualified PDK primitive still requires its own model.

theory_records.title: Polynomial additive-unit model
theory_records.claim: Under an additive identical-unit parameter model, equal spatial moments through n cancel every polynomial component of degree at most n.
theory_records.assumptions: Two identically designed devices; parameter additivity; unit center approximates area average, or finite-footprint equivalence is independently justified.

theory_records.title: Recursive central-symmetry parity
theory_records.claim: Reflect the prior pattern, retaining labels for odd target order and exchanging labels for even target order; the specified base leads to 2^n units per device.
theory_records.locator: §III recursive construction and induction, printed pp.4836–4837
theory_records.assumptions: First-order base has two units per device; legal disjoint placement; not a minimal-count or circuit-performance theorem.

theory_records.title: DAC plate identities and parasitic classes
theory_records.claim: Binary and split DAC networks respond differently to top/substrate, top/bottom and bottom/substrate parasitics; split banks retain two top-plate nodes.
theory_records.assumptions: Specified charge-scaling architecture and ideal static excitation conditions; dynamic reference/switch effects require extensions.

theory_records.title: Constructive DAC families and odd counts
theory_records.claim: Spiral/chessboard/block choices trade connected components against dispersion; the two one-unit members are deliberately only near the common center.
theory_records.assumptions: Identical nonoverlapping grid units; preserve exact electrical counts and quantify CC exceptions.

theory_records.title: DAC routing construction
theory_records.claim: Same-bit components are joined by branch/trunk/bridge routes; top plates use graph/MST routing, separately for split-bank nodes.
theory_records.assumptions: Specified layer/pin/array model; MST wire cost does not prove minimum electrical delay.

theory_records.title: DAC INL and DNL definitions
theory_records.claim: DNL evaluates adjacent output steps relative to one ideal LSB; INL evaluates deviation from the declared ideal transfer.
theory_records.assumptions: Record reference convention, code endpoints and normalization; endpoint or best-fit corrections change the metric.

theory_records.title: Paper-specific DAC frequency
theory_records.claim: The paper’s Eq.(32) defines f=1/[2(N+2)ln(2)τ] from its charging/discharging model.
theory_records.assumptions: τ is the worst modeled charging-path delay. This N-dependent settling measure must not be equated to 1/(2πτ).

theory_records.title: MOM bridge edge sensitivity
theory_records.claim: For a common small edge displacement δ, the specified MOM geometry gives ΔC/C≈2δ(1/H+1/l), enabling joint nominal-C and fractional-sensitivity matching.
theory_records.assumptions: H and l are in-plane dimensions; common small perturbation, continuous geometry, and simplified coupling model. Quantization/fringing require extraction.

theory_records.title: Do not promote illustrative correlation to process data
theory_records.claim: The DAC evaluation’s gradient/correlation constants are inherited assumptions, not a measured capacitor statistical characterization.
theory_records.locator: §V setup and parameter discussion, printed pp.2791,2793
theory_records.assumptions: Yield/correlation claims require qualified process data; parameter sweeps study conditional behavior only.

theory_records.title: Widening shifts the critical bit
theory_records.claim: Parallel critical-bit routes can improve delay but change the bottleneck and eventually have diminishing returns.
theory_records.assumptions: Re-evaluate all bits with changed capacitance, vias and routing capacity; numerical gains belong to that setup.

theory_records.title: Electrical feedback closes a proxy gap
theory_records.claim: Geometric constraints and scalar physical objectives do not generally guarantee post-layout circuit performance.
theory_records.assumptions: Contract and testbench determine required metrics. An extracted/simulated result is conditional on model coverage.

theory_records.title: Model cost needs consistent denominators
theory_records.claim: The survey’s text and Fig.2 have inconsistent runtime fractions; only the qualitative data-acquisition-dominance lesson is safely reused.
theory_records.assumptions: Apparent internal inconsistency, visually checked; not a publisher-verified erratum or an engine runtime budget.

theory_records.title: Transfer accuracy is metric/domain dependent
theory_records.claim: The transfer example behaves differently for bandwidth, CMRR and noise across sizing/topology changes.
theory_records.assumptions: Reported circuits and train/test domains; no generalization guarantee beyond them.

theory_records.title: Retain competing objectives
theory_records.claim: The MOBO/weighted-BO comparison motivates considering tradeoffs among circuit metrics.
theory_records.assumptions: Reported case study. A feasible Pareto archive is our software policy and is not a global-frontier proof.

theory_records.title: Discrete per-net wire sizing
theory_records.claim: The manuscript assigns integer width choices per net after global routing; symmetric nets receive equal width choices.
theory_records.assumptions: Metrics in normalized ratio scores must have meaningful positive values; final feasibility remains separate from weighted FOM.

theory_records.title: WAGN physical graph features
theory_records.claim: Pins and route Steiner nodes carry device/role/geometry features; edges include distance, via count, widths, pin dimensions and terminal types.
theory_records.assumptions: These are the reported model inputs, not proof that any particular graph network is needed for this engine.

theory_records.title: WAGN output is a threshold classifier
theory_records.claim: The model output is denoted P(FOM<T) at one specified threshold and trained with binary labels/cross entropy.
theory_records.assumptions: Not a full CDF, metric regression or established calibration/yield model; observed classification accuracy does not supply those guarantees.

theory_records.title: Simulated shortlist after surrogate search
theory_records.claim: Relax/search widths through fixed WAGN, discretize, and simulate the top shortlist before final selection.
theory_records.assumptions: Multistart/local/BO methods are heuristic; finite penalty, rounding and route fallback require actual feasibility checks.

theory_records.title: Parallel routes implement width options
theory_records.claim: The experiments implement 1×, 2× and 3× width choices using parallel routes.
theory_records.assumptions: The realized route graph may differ from a single wide conductor; routability and access remain conditional.

theory_records.title: Wider can improve one metric and hurt another
theory_records.claim: Table7’s CM-OTA 1×→3× change raises UGF 451.0→511.4 MHz while reducing gain 33.1→31.1 dB and FOM 0.92→0.90.
theory_records.assumptions: One reported circuit/setup; do not reuse the numbers as a target-process forecast.

theory_records.title: WAGN evidence and stated limits
theory_records.claim: Runtime/gain claims compare specified BO budgets; the paper limits cross-family transfer, large circuits, process variation and classification-only prediction.
theory_records.assumptions: Training-data cost, parallel hardware and circuit family must accompany comparisons; no experiments reproduced here.

theory_records.title: Weighted and ratio centroid extension
theory_records.claim: For additive nominal contributions wi sharing the same fractional spatial field, normalized device response uses Σwi p(ri)/Σwi; matched normalized first moments cancel a linear field.
theory_records.locator: Derived extension of Eqs.(1)–(5), not a quoted weighted-ratio theorem
theory_records.assumptions: Additive electrical composition; weights defined for the actual absolute/fractional perturbation; sensitivities and bias compatible.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Expand p=p0+gx x+gy y in each normalized sum and subtract. Unequal counts are valid after normalization; arbitrary model sensitivities may not be simple positive area weights.

theory_records.title: Finite-footprint polynomial certificate
theory_records.claim: Identical translated unit footprints preserve moment cancellation through n when their center moments match through n.
theory_records.assumptions: Identical footprint weighting kernels; linear/additive field response; same internal moments for all units.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Integrate (xi+u)^a(yi+v)^b over a common normalized footprint. Binomial expansion yields products of center moments of degree ≤a+b and common internal moments; all differential terms vanish when the corresponding center moments match.

theory_records.title: Single-branch source degeneration
theory_records.claim: gm,eff=gm/(1+gmRs) under a restricted one-branch small-signal model.
theory_records.locator: Derived from the mechanism in §V-A Eq.(25); the closed form is not printed there
theory_records.assumptions: Neglect gds/body effect; source-resistor current equals modeled branch current; gm is local and constant.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: i=gm(vin−iRs) gives i(1+gmRs)=gm vin; divide by vin. A multi-unit array requires its actual current distribution.

theory_records.title: Linear RC nodal stamp
theory_records.claim: A physical capacitor c between i and j stamps +c diagonals and −c off-diagonals; KCL yields Gv+C dv/dt=i for the linear RC network.
theory_records.locator: Circuit-law derivation; §2.5.3 provides RC modeling background, not this matrix formula
theory_records.assumptions: Linear passive elements; identified reference/boundary nodes; capacitance convention fixed. Ideal voltage sources/inductors need additional treatment.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: q_i=c(v_i−v_j), q_j=−q_i; differentiate and sum terminal currents. Resistor currents are (v_i−v_j)/R. This derivation supplies the stamp rather than a purported source quotation.

theory_records.title: Fast capacitive charge sharing
theory_records.claim: For a floating victim with quiet-node Cv and aggressor coupling Cc, ΔVv=Cc/(Cv+Cc)ΔVa.
theory_records.locator: Independent charge-conservation derivation; substrate electroquasistatics is background only
theory_records.assumptions: Ideal fast imposed aggressor step; fixed quiet reference; no charge escape or other changing coupled nodes; linear C.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Conserve victim charge: CvΔVv+Cc(ΔVv−ΔVa)=0. Finite driver impedance or nonlinear clamps require transient analysis.

theory_records.title: Toy finite optimal wire width
theory_records.claim: For τ(w)=(Rd+a/w)(CL+bw) with positive parameters, the continuous optimum is sqrt(aCL/(Rd b)), before legal bounds/discretization.
theory_records.locator: Original illustrative model motivated by RC tradeoffs, not the manuscript objective
theory_records.assumptions: Rd,b,a,CL>0; fixed topology; C varies linearly and R inversely with width; single time-constant objective.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: dτ/dw=Rd b−aCL/w²; d²τ/dw²=2aCL/w³>0. With Rd=0 or b=0 and other terms positive there is no finite stationary optimum of this form.

theory_records.title: Johnson–Nyquist foundational citation gap
theory_records.claim: The glossary states classical one-sided resistor voltage PSD 4kBTR; no exact supporting equation was located in the supplied corpus.
theory_records.locator: Foundational law with no verified corpus locator
theory_records.assumptions: Equilibrium passive resistor, classical frequency regime, one-sided PSD in V²/Hz. The formula itself is a background assumption in this handbook.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Conditional consistency check: filtering 4kBTR by 1/[1+(2πfRC)²] and integrating f≥0 gives kBT/C. This integration does not independently prove the underlying thermal-noise law.

theory_records.title: Equilibrium sampled-capacitor noise
theory_records.claim: One ideal equilibrated linear capacitor has voltage variance kBT/C.
theory_records.locator: Independent equipartition derivation; no exact supplied-PDF kT/C passage located
theory_records.assumptions: One thermalized degree of freedom, classical equilibrium, no incomplete settling or correlated-sampling modification; a full DAC has other transfer factors.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Equipartition gives ½C Var(v)=½kBT, so Var(v)=kBT/C. Foundational equipartition premise is assumed; do not cite the DAC paper as the source of this formula.

theory_records.title: Zero failures do not prove zero failure rate
theory_records.claim: For n independent representative Bernoulli trials with zero failures, a one-sided 1−α upper bound is 1−α^(1/n), approximately −ln(α)/n.
theory_records.assumptions: Independent identically distributed outcomes and a fixed acceptance event; not weighted importance samples or adaptive/censored failures.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: P(no failures|p)=(1−p)^n. Invert at α. At 95% confidence and n=1000 the upper bound is about 0.00299125 (0.2991%).

theory_records.title: Half-LSB single-pole settling
theory_records.claim: For a full-scale single-pole step and half an N-bit LSB residual, t≥(N+1)ln(2)τ.
theory_records.locator: Original exponential-settling derivation; distinct from source Eq.(32)
theory_records.assumptions: Single pole; unit full-scale initial error; half-LSB allocation; no slew/ringing or other error consuming the allocation.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Require exp(−t/τ)≤2^(−N−1), take logs. This is not a sample-rate certificate for an arbitrary switched array.

theory_records.title: Constraint instance and provenance contract
theory_records.claim: Store the physical mechanism, targets, units, scope, parent requirement, model provenance, enforcement and evidence for each proposed rule.
theory_records.assumptions: The 84 rule families are proposals to instantiate, not author-numbered textbook rules or universal foundry limits.

theory_records.title: Coverage and evidence freshness
theory_records.claim: Distinguish pass/fail/unknown/not-applicable and invalidate checks when their geometry/model/scenario inputs change.
theory_records.assumptions: Acceptance requires every selected mandatory evaluator to run successfully within its domain; no claim that a cited book prescribes this exact software schema.

theory_records.title: Search guarantee and selection policy
theory_records.claim: Distinguish best observed, nondominated among evaluated, and proven optimum within a restricted representation.
theory_records.assumptions: Proof scope is limited by the represented feasible set, objective, model and solver evidence; a failed heuristic is not infeasibility proof.

theory_records.title: Fault detectability differs from fault incidence
theory_records.claim: Layouts with equal expected defect faults can differ in detectability; the source weights routing exposure using good/faulty response separation.
theory_records.assumptions: A specified fault model, stimulus and response distribution are required. Inverse statistical distance is a cost proxy, not a calibrated escape probability; accepting a hypothesis does not establish posterior probability that an individual circuit is good.

unresolved.detail: No exact Johnson–Nyquist 4kBTR or kT/C equation locator found in the supplied PDFs. Labeled foundation and derived respectively; do not attribute to these DAC/layout papers.

Semantic source review is not proof of every proposition in every book, reproduction of source experiments or qualification for a target PDK. Algorithm contracts and validation procedures remain handbook proposals.
